IE 7275 — Data Mining in Engineering | prerequisites, offerings, professors (Northeastern)

NU Map is an independent, student-built planner — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data comes from the public catalog on a schedule; confirm with the official catalog and an advisor.

4 semester hoursGraduateLectureusually offered: fall, spring, summerBostonOnlineSeattle, WAVancouver, CanadaLive CastOnlineTraditional

Covers the theory and applications of data mining in engineering. Reviews fundamentals and key concepts of data mining, discusses important data mining techniques, and presents algorithms for implementing these techniques. Specifically covers data mining techniques for data preprocessing, association rule extraction, classification, prediction, clustering, and complex data exploration. Discusses data mining applications in several areas, including manufacturing, healthcare, medicine, business, and other service sectors.

(CS 5800 (min C) or EECE 7205 (min C) or IE 5374 (min C) or IE 5374 (min D) or IE 6200 (min C) or IE 6400 (min C) or MATH 7241 (min C))
